claims.text: Conventional aluminum alloys are used in aerospace and automotive applications.
An aluminum alloy can be reinforced with 1–5 vol% SiC or TiC nanoparticles using high-energy ball milling followed by hot pressing.
Ceramic nanoparticle incorporation refines the aluminum-alloy microstructure.
Dispersed ceramic nanoparticles form nanoscale obstacles to dislocation motion in the aluminum matrix.
The ceramic nanoparticles hinder dislocation movement.
Nanoparticle-induced grain refinement and impeded dislocation motion enhance mechanical strength.
Nanoparticle-induced grain refinement and impeded dislocation motion enhance durability.
Ceramic nanoparticle reinforcement improves the thermal stability of the aluminum alloy.
Adding 1–5 vol% ceramic nanoparticles allows the material to maintain low density.
The nanoparticle-reinforced aluminum alloy will have greater tensile strength than the unreinforced alloy.
The nanoparticle-reinforced aluminum alloy will have greater fatigue resistance than the unreinforced alloy.
The nanoparticle-reinforced aluminum alloy will have better thermal stability than the unreinforced alloy.
The predicted performance improvements will not compromise the alloy's lightweight nature.
Nanoparticle agglomeration is a potential limitation of the proposed approach.
Scaling the proposed ball-milling and hot-pressing process may be difficult.
Ceramic nanoparticle contents above 5 vol% could make the aluminum composite brittle.
